--- TestEVEUpgradeKubevirtToKubevirt ---
timed out after 10m0.016354381s (excluding download) waiting for app "72832e16-11d3-42f6-adc3-9fe739eb7ce8" (upgrade-test-app) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: HALTING)

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

This is the same known `TestEVEUpgradeKubevirtToKubevirt` bug documented repeatedly in the ledger. Live `domainmgr` logs on `edge-dev` show `doActivate` for `upgrade-test-app` hit `failed calling webhook "virtualmachinereplicaset-validator.kubevirt.io": ... dial tcp 10.43.165.149:443: connect: connection refused` at 02:31:10 (right after the post-baseos-upgrade reboot cycle, while `virt-api`'s pod sandbox was being recreated), driving the app to `HALTING`. `kubectl get pods -n kubevirt` now shows `virt-api` healthy and `Running` (1 restart, ~10m ago), but `kubectl get vmi,vm,vmirs -A` returns "No resources found" — no VM/VMI/VMIRS was ever (re)created. `domainmgr`'s log since the single webhook failure shows only a `maybeRetryBoot(72832e16-...) N remaining` countdown ticking down every few seconds (196 → 43 and falling) with no further `handleCreate`/`doActivate`/webhook-call attempt, meaning the retry timer is counting down but never re-driving actual VMIRS/VMI creation even though the webhook backend has been reachable again for minutes.

This exact signature (one-shot webhook failure right after post-upgrade reboot + retry countdown that never re-attempts creation) is extensively recorded in `live-ledger.md` as a known/recurring issue for this specific test, first seen 2026-11-19 and reproduced again on 2026-11-22 and in multiple runs since — tonight's occurrence is a continuation of that same long-standing `domainmgr` retry-logic bug, not a new regression. The broker (`farfalle`) shows modest CPU load (8%, load ~6.5/40 CPUs) though VM memory is overcommitted at 111% of host RAM; this isn't clearly implicated here since the failure mode (stuck countdown, no retry) matches the known code-level bug rather than a resource-starvation symptom. No PR diff was supplied, so no relatedness verdict is given.

--- TestThreeNodesUpgrade ---
Timed out waiting for cluster nodes to become ready in cluster "test-cluster" (device "edge-dev2")

Claude's conclusion:
This confirms the exact same race condition documented previously: all three nodes independently hit "Single node mode prepare config.yaml" within the same second (02:52:43–02:52:44), each bootstrapping its own single-node k3s instead of joining a shared cluster.

Root cause: Live evidence shows all three nodes (`edge-dev1`, `edge-dev2`, `edge-dev3`) independently fell into k3s single-node bootstrap mode — `/persist/kubelog/k3s-install.log` on all three shows `First time for k3s install` / `Single node mode prepare config.yaml for <node>` within the same second (02:52:43–02:52:44), confirming `cluster-init.sh`'s first-boot check lost the race against zedkube processing the `EdgeNodeClusterConfig` on every node. `evetest cluster info` corroborates this live: each node reports its own distinct `node_id` and only itself in its node set (though sharing the same `cluster_id`), with storage health flapping between `SERVICE_STATUS_HEALTHY`/`SERVICE_STATUS_FAILED` — consistent with each node independently standing up its own full kubevirt/longhorn stack, which is why `evetest status` reports "Timed out waiting for cluster nodes to become ready" on `edge-dev2`.

This is unrelated to the earlier `TestEVEUpgradeKubevirtToKubevirt` failure investigated in this run (that was a one-shot webhook-connectivity/retry-countdown bug in `domainmgr`, a different test and mechanism). Per the ledger, this is a well-established **known, recurring issue** for `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` specifically — the identical "every node independently races into k3s single-node bootstrap mode before zedkube applies `EdgeNodeClusterConfig`" signature was first recorded 2026-11-19 (run #26) and has recurred repeatedly since (e.g. 2026-11-26/run #57), so tonight's failure is a continuation of that same long-standing `cluster-init.sh`/zedkube race, not a new regression.

--- TestThreeNodesUpgrade ---
Timed out after 902.244s.
The function passed to Eventually failed at /evetest/tests/upgrade/cluster_upgrade_test.go:191 with:
Unexpected error:
    <*fmt.wrapError | 0x3c70b29ee3a0>: 
    unable to reach app "6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c" SSH on device "edge-dev1": no reachable endpoint among [172.20.20.226:2222]
    {
        msg: "unable to reach app \"6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c\" SSH on device \"edge-dev1\": no reachable endpoint among [172.20.20.226:2222]",
        err: <*errors.errorString | 0x3c70b236e230>{
            s: "no reachable endpoint among [172.20.20.226:2222]",
        },
    }
occurred

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live inspection of `upgrade-app` (`6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c`) across all three nodes shows it's healthy, just not where the test is polling. On `edge-dev1` its `app-info` history ends in two consecutive `state:INITIAL` entries (no more BOOTING/RUNNING events after ~748236s), while `edge-dev3`'s `app-info` shows the same app reached `state:RUNNING` with pod IP `10.11.12.2` just afterward (`bootTime:1795748319`). This is the classic rolling-upgrade VMI eviction pattern: `edge-dev1` was cordoned/drained/rebooted for its baseos upgrade, the VMIRS evicted the app from it and rescheduled it onto `edge-dev3`, but the test's fixed SSH target (`cluster_upgrade_test.go:191`) kept polling `edge-dev1`'s `172.20.20.226:2222`, which genuinely has nothing listening for the app anymore — hence the 902s timeout.

This is the same mechanism already documented once before in the ledger under `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` (SSH-reach timeout against `edge-dev1:172.20.20.226:2222`, app actually relocated to `edge-dev2` in that case) — attributed there to a harness gap (fixed-device polling instead of resolving the node currently hosting a migrated app), similar to a recurring `FindDeviceHostingApp` bug seen for a different test. It is not one of the other previously-logged `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` failure modes (k3s single-node-bootstrap race, Proxmox `qmcreate` ZFS-lock timeout) — those have different signatures. Broker status shows the host at 105% memory overcommit but swap usage is low (0.5/8 GiB), so this doesn't look environment-driven tonight. No PR diff was supplied for this investigation.

It happens entirely during the app's first volume creation on a freshly-installed device, before any base-image upgrade/reboot step, so it's unrelated to the upgrade machinery itself — the slow/stalled persist-disk I/O during containerd unpack is the proximate cause each night, pointing at underlying host storage contention rather than a pillar code defect.

Claude's conclusion:
This matches exactly the overloaded single-node k3s symptom seen before (cdi crash-looping, longhorn pods stuck in ContainerCreating). I have enough evidence to conclude.

**Root cause:** All three `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` nodes independently fell into k3s single-node bootstrap mode instead of joining as a single cluster. Live evidence: `k3s-install.log` on all three devices shows `First time for k3s install` / `Single node mode prepare config.yaml for <node>` within 2 seconds of each other (edge-dev1 03:04:18, edge-dev2 03:04:18, edge-dev3 03:04:20), and `kubectl get nodes` on each device independently shows only itself as `Ready control-plane` rather than a shared 3-node cluster — the exact same `cluster-init.sh` first-boot race against zedkube's `EdgeNodeClusterConfig` processing documented before. --- TestEVEUpgradeKubevirtToKubevirt ---
Timed out after 1200.001s.
When passed a matcher, ReceiveMatcher's channel *must* receive something.

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

The device's single-node k3s cluster became `kubelet`-Ready at the Kubernetes level, but the kubevirt/CDI/longhorn control plane was still not converged 20 minutes later — live `kubectl get pods -A` shows `cdi-apiserver`, `cdi-deployment`, `cdi-uploadproxy` still `ContainerCreating`, and there's no `longhorn-system` namespace at all. Local device logs confirm `domainmgr` was still blocked at `04:20:40` (the very end of the window) with `"WaitForKubernetes not satisfied... kubevirt not ready: KubeVirt CR not yet Available"`, and `zedkube`'s `collectKubeStats()` was failing every ~30s with `"can't get VMIs the server could not find the requested resource (get virtualmachineinstances.kubevirt.io)"` — per `pkg/pillar/cmd/zedkube/kubestatscollect.go`, that error makes the function `return` before ever calling `pubKubeClusterInfo.Publish`, so `zedagent` never had anything new to forward to the controller. This is corroborated live: Adam has zero `ZiKubeCluster` info messages for this device across the entire run, which is why the test's `Eventually(clusterUpdates, 20m).Should(Receive(...))` never saw a value and ultimately failed with the gomega `ReceiveMatcher` error instead of a plain timeout.

This does **not** share a root cause with this run's earlier `TestEVEUpgradeKVMtoKVM` failure (that was an unrelated containerd `Image.Unpack` hang on a KVM device, with no kubevirt involvement). It does, however, belong to the same known, recurring failure class already in the ledger for this exact test: an overloaded single-node k3s VM failing to converge its kubevirt+CDI+longhorn control plane within the test's timeout, first seen 2026-11-19 (stuck `HALTING` on a post-upgrade `virt-api` webhook stall) and again on 2026-11-22/run #37 (`volumemgr` blocked on `WaitForKubernetes`/longhorn readiness). Tonight's manifestation — zero cluster-info ever published, causing a gomega `Receive`-matcher error instead of a plain state-timeout — is a new surface symptom of that same underlying resource-contention/convergence-speed problem, not a previously-recorded exact signature.

--- TestThreeNodesUpgrade ---
Failed to setup devices [edge-dev1 edge-dev2 edge-dev3]: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to reconfigure disks for device "edge-dev1" after installation: failed to detach disk virtio0 from device "eve-547dcb59-edge-dev1": bad request: 400 Parameter verification failed. - {"virtio0":"unable to apply pending change virtio0 : can't lock file '/var/lock/pve-manager/pve-storage-farfalle-pve-zfs-pool' - got timeout\n"}, EVE installation timed out or failed for device "edge-dev3", EVE installation timed out or failed for device "edge-dev2"

Claude's conclusion:
Confirms no EVE devices ever came up (consistent with a pure host-side provisioning failure before pillar ever ran).

**Root cause:** This is a Proxmox host-side storage-lock contention failure on the `farfalle` host, not an EVE/pillar defect — `edge-dev1` failed the post-install disk-reconfigure step (detaching `virtio0`) because it couldn't acquire `/var/lock/pve-manager/pve-storage-farfalle-pve-zfs-pool` within Proxmox's internal timeout, while `edge-dev2`/`edge-dev3`'s installations simply timed out, consistent with concurrent VM provisioning for all three nodes contending for the same ZFS-pool lock on `farfalle`.
